match.reason: The closest card, Gaps and niches in the market, covers finding gaps by listening to customers and noticing complaints, but it leaves out new technology and changes in how people live, and it centres on niche markets, so it is narrower than this point; the Business Management card is aimed at VCE rather than Year 7-8.

draft.title: Spotting a market opportunity
card: A market opportunity is an unmet need or a gap in what is on offer. A business that can fill it has a chance to gain customers.
Market research
asking people or studying data to learn what customers want. A survey that shows many families cannot find a product shows a gap.
New technology
can make something possible that was not possible before, or make it cheaper. This can open a gap for a new product or service.
Changes in how people live
such as more people working from home, can create needs that no business is meeting yet.
draft.remember: A market opportunity is a gap a business can fill. Research, technology and changing lives can reveal one.

a.q: Which of these is a market opportunity?
opts: Many shoppers want a service that no local business offers
A shop owner wants to earn more money this year
A business has hired three extra staff members
A café has a wide range of drinks on its menu
a.why: A market opportunity is an unmet need or gap that a business can fill. Wanting more money is a goal of the owner, not a gap in what customers can buy.
a.clue: Look for a need that nobody is meeting yet.

b.q: Jess runs a small shop in Bendigo. She asks 100 local people what they would like to buy, and many say they cannot find fresh bread made without gluten. What has Jess done?
opts: Used market research to spot a market opportunity
Used new technology to spot a market opportunity
Spotted a market opportunity from a change in lifestyle
Set a goal of growing her share of the market
b.why: Jess asked people what they want, which is market research. Their answers show a gap that she could fill. She did not use new technology, and the card does not say that people's way of life changed.
b.clue: How did Jess find out what customers want?

a.best: Many shoppers want a service that no local business offers

b.best: Used market research to spot a market opportunity
